title: SubatlasScores
description: How every atlas cell set overlaps the cell sets of each contributing study, measured deterministically from a CAS+ document's transferred_annotations. Two independent groupings of the same cells are in play and are never conflated: an ATLAS CELL SET is one the atlas defines (an annotations[] entry, named by cell_label); a SUBATLAS CELL SET is one a contributing study defines (named by transferred_cell_label), whose size 'as integrated' is however many of its cells reached the atlas. Derived, not authored — regenerate with `python -m atlas_chat.cli_subatlas_scores` rather than hand-editing.

cas_source.description: Path to the CAS+ document this was computed from.

atlas_doi.description: The atlas paper's DOI, copied from source.doi.

degraded.description: True when no usable partition was found, so fraction_of_subatlas_set and f1 could not be computed and the cutoff fell back to purity alone. A degraded run is a coverage limit, not a finding about the data.

sensitivity.description: How the surviving set changes across candidate f1 floors. Recorded because the f1 distribution has no knee, so any floor is a policy choice: a later change should be a diff against this table, not an argument.

cell_sets.description: One entry per atlas cell set carrying transferred_annotations. Atlas cell sets with no provenance are omitted entirely.

unpublished.description: Contributing studies with real provenance but no DOI — nothing to read, held apart from studies excluded for being small.

Partition.description: The set of atlas cell sets used to size each subatlas cell set atlas-wide: it must cover every cell exactly once. Found, never assumed — annotation is not always hierarchical, and a labelset does not always cover the atlas.

basis.description: 'hierarchy_leaves' = atlas cell sets that are no other cell set's parent (these may span several labelsets, which is why 'the finest labelset' is the wrong rule); 'labelset' = one whole labelset, used when no parent links exist; 'none' = no usable partition, so the run is degraded.

total_cells.description: Cells covered by the partition. This is the atlas total by construction.

labelsets_spanned.description: Labelsets the partition's cell sets come from. More than one is normal for hierarchy_leaves.

reason.description: Why no partition was usable, when basis is 'none' — e.g. cell sets missing n_cells, or candidate labelsets whose totals disagree.

Thresholds.description: Recorded on every run so a threshold change is visible as a diff.

f1_floor.description: Minimum f1 for an overlap to reach the read plan.

min_overlap_cells.description: Minimum overlap_cells, guarding against reading a correspondence into a handful of cells.

purity_floor.description: Fallback gate used only on a degraded run, where f1 does not exist.

record_floor.description: Overlaps whose purity falls below this are rolled into the tail rather than listed individually. A recording economy, not a judgement: the tail names every study it aggregated.

shape_high.description: Above this a ratio counts as high when reading off overlap_shape. Deliberately separate from f1_floor: whether an overlap is worth asking about and whether it looks one-to-one are different judgements, and reusing the inclusion floor for both called a 0.39/0.29 overlap one_to_one.

cell_label.description: The atlas's own name for this cell set.

n_cells.description: Cells in this atlas cell set, from every source. Used only for fraction_of_atlas_set — never as a denominator for purity.

synonyms.description: The atlas cell set's CAS+ synonyms, carried through because a synonym naming a subatlas cell set force-includes that overlap regardless of f1.

tail.description: Overlaps below record_floor, aggregated per contributing study so an exclusion stays visible.

Overlap.description: One atlas cell set's intersection with one subatlas cell set.

subatlas_paper.description: Registry key — matches a source.subatlas_papers[].label, or the raw source_taxonomy where no registry entry exists.

doi.description: The contributing study's DOI, when known. Absent for a source with no publication.

subatlas_cell_label.description: The contributing study's own name for its cell set.

source_labelset.description: The upstream labelset (obs column) this name came from.

overlap_cells.description: Cells belonging to both this atlas cell set and this subatlas cell set.

subatlas_contribution_cells.description: Every cell of this atlas cell set that came from this study, whatever the study called it. The denominator for purity.

subatlas_set_total_cells.description: This subatlas cell set's size across the whole atlas, summed over the partition. The denominator for fraction_of_subatlas_set. Absent on a degraded run.

purity.description: overlap_cells / subatlas_contribution_cells — of what this study contributed to this atlas cell set, the fraction that is this one subatlas cell set. The denominator is deliberately the study's contribution and NOT n_cells: most cells here usually came from other studies that never saw them, and counting those would penalise a study for cells it had no part in. Called within_source_share on the subatlas-consistency branch.

fraction_of_subatlas_set.description: overlap_cells / subatlas_set_total_cells — of this subatlas cell set, the fraction that landed here. High means this atlas cell set accounts for it; low means it was spread across several. Called reverse_share on the subatlas-consistency branch. Absent on a degraded run.

fraction_of_atlas_set.description: overlap_cells / n_cells — of this atlas cell set, the fraction that is this subatlas cell set. RECORDED, NEVER GATED: it is confounded by every other study's cells, so a low value says more about how many studies fed this cell set than about the correspondence.

f1.description: Harmonic mean of fraction_of_subatlas_set and purity — high only when both are, which is what a one-to-one correspondence requires. Neither alone suffices: on the reference project 575 overlaps have fraction_of_subatlas_set >= 0.9 and 405 of those have purity < 0.5, being coarse atlas cell sets that absorbed a fine subatlas one whole. Absent on a degraded run.

OverlapShape.description: The shape of the overlap, read off the two ratios alone — it says what to ask the paper, not what the answer is. 'one_to_one' = both high. 'atlas_set_within_subatlas_set' = purity high, fraction_of_subatlas_set low: the atlas split the subatlas cell set and this is one piece. 'subatlas_set_within_atlas_set' = the reverse: this atlas cell set absorbed the subatlas one along with others from the same study, so agreement here is a resolution difference and not corroboration. 'weak' = both low. 'unknown' = degraded run, no partition.

UnpublishedContributor.description: A contributing study with provenance but no DOI. Named at setup so it is a known gap before any reading is attempted, rather than a surprise mid-run.

status.description: Ingest route from the registry, when present.
